issue: Opaque tile-like ice and busy body tracery.
rationale: Raised floes, blue leads and rear ice blocks remain readable. Accept the enamel-like miniature interpretation, not promotional translucency; tiny ponds and hinge seating remain unresolved at this scale.

issue: Low faceted ridge rather than craggy promotional relief.
rationale: Individual-board inspection resolves two low angular banks around a crooked cyan rift. The split-ridge motif survives; reduced height, graphic waves and uncertain physical channel depth are disclosed rather than treated as missing terrain.

issue: Regular sandstone bands and faceted domes.
rationale: Five banded domes preserve Bungle Bungle identity. Natural weathering and irregular strata are reduced; this is coherent miniature stylization, not loss of the landform.

issue: Botanical medallion differs from promotional radial ornament.
rationale: The circular botanical relief remains a distinct lid focal point on a copper-colored chest. Accept this ornamental interpretation with disclosed non-equivalence, mottled orange finish and weak hammered-metal response.

issue: Dense speckling obscures individual fossil rings.
rationale: Pale branching fossil relief and blue-gray stone body remain recognizable. Angular fossil detail and flatter brass are ordinary stylized finish limitations, without a demonstrated missing motif.

issue: Broad mountain facets and plaster/timber material reading.
rationale: Painted cream/red panels, layered cornice and projecting mountain are preserved. Accept the deliberately schematic mountain rather than demand promotional crag detail or woven/leather realism; exact material equivalence is not claimed.

issue: Thin salt polygons and plank-like white courses.
rationale: Pale-blue polygon field and ochre mound communicate the salt-flat miniature. Crystalline halite realism and strong lattice depth are absent from the visual impression, but the intended abstraction remains legible.

issue: Matte copper coating and thin schematic floral loops.
rationale: Rosette, beaded border and intentional patina seam remain visible. Accept disclosed wire-outline petals and copper-colored coating; no claim of authentic hammered artisan work or verified hinge mechanics.

issue: Sparse repeated crowns and weak small-scale river contrast.
rationale: Individual-board inspection retains a pale curved channel between tree belts. Accept a schematic wooded-river diorama, not dense naturalistic Amazon canopy; continuous water is harder to trace at phone scale, but the winding river is not demonstrated absent.

issue: Burgundy saturation and flat repetitive gold diamonds.
rationale: Gold-on-burgundy patterned textile identity is clear in closed and open views. Muted promotional brocade, tactile threads and irregularity are not reproduced; those finish differences do not require a taste hold.

issue: Soft streaked stone and rounded canopy.
rationale: Fako peak and surrounding green vegetation remain recognizable. Cooler granular volcanic-stone realism is weaker, but the miniature terrain is coherent; apparent hinge spacing is not proof of detachment.

issue: Tiny pond and simplified lobed trees.
rationale: Trees around the pale clearing preserve Dzanga identity; small blue water detail is weak, not proven absent. The review describes a pond, not a required extended river, so failure to read as a river is not a valid new requirement.

issue: Bulbous floral clusters and bright banded red finish.
rationale: Raised peony-like clusters and red/gold ornamental identity survive. Fine stems, leaves and carved centers are less legible; accept this miniature relief without promising promotional lacquer or exact flower detail.

issue: Graphic caustic-like veining rather than cloudy mineral depth.
rationale: Blue-white larimar palette, lid stones and pale feet remain distinct. Dense repeating veins and angular transitions are disclosed surface stylization, not missing stone ornament.

issue: Saturated geometric tile palette replaces softer floral treatment.
rationale: Multicolor tiled lid remains a coherent focal point on the pale chest. Accept stronger green/red/ochre geometry with weak glaze and grout depth; do not describe it as an exact pastel floral replica.

issue: Coarse snow facets and regular masonry.
rationale: Tower, snow peaks and green ground are legible in closed views. Marketing is itself stylized; reduced speckling and irregular joints do not establish missing terrain or justify a photorealism gate.

issue: Regular village platform and fine repetitive wood grain.
rationale: Red-roofed houses and turned trees retain the woodcraft miniature theme. Weak wood/brass separation and flat carrier are ordinary polish limitations, not absent architecture.

issue: Gray stone lid/feet and deeper indigo than promotion.
rationale: Three volcano forms and turquoise lake remain readable above striped body panels. Accept the darker material allocation with flat water and stripe-based textile abstraction; no claim of exact blue-foot or woven-material fidelity.

issue: Flat crowded botanical relief and repetitive blue mottling.
rationale: Oval garden foliage remains visible on the closed lid. Accept schematic cut-steel-inspired ornament, disclosing reduced depth and leaf readability rather than claiming sculptural promotional richness.

issue: Pale lid, opaque lagoon and ambiguous hinge silhouette.
rationale: Broken ivory atoll arcs and lagoon remain recognizable. Four channels are not equally resolved in stills, not shown missing. Accept brighter/paler finish; continuous mechanics and hidden attachment remain unverified, not cleared by this visual decision.

issue: Named copper openwork is not reliably legible in actual closed views.
rationale: Individual-board inspection and independent review agree that five rosettes reduce to weak yellow marks against a washed-out lid; open-loop structure, thickness and separation cannot be established at displayed scale. Retain a substantive named-feature readability hold, not a demand for shinier metal or proof that meshes are absent.

issue: Regular small limestone blocks and broad cream marble waves.
rationale: Raised limestone pavement and green marble-like chest remain legible. Accept tidy block geometry and lighter ring weight as miniature simplification; no exact natural limestone or fine promotional contour match is claimed.

issue: Saturated terracotta bands and schematic siq inlay.
rationale: Two fluted massifs and open arch remain readable. Accept the warm rose/ochre stylization, broad wood-like strata and thin inlay rather than an excavated gorge; pale promotional stone is not the actual finish and must not be represented as equivalent.

issue: Crimson versus mauve palette and weak woven-thread relief.
rationale: Body lattice and distinct lid diamonds preserve Songket-inspired identity. Accept graphic gold patterning and altered inset contrast with aliasing disclosed; no authentic raised-thread material claim or hinge certification follows.

issue: Regular masonry and opaque turquoise canal inserts.
rationale: Platforms, stacked architecture and channels remain clear. Accept stylized basalt/canal scene with less grain and softer promotional bases explicitly not reproduced; water realism is not required for the miniature.

issue: Compact village on lower regular shelf.
rationale: Coastal village, blue water and red body graphics survive. Accept smaller footprint and simplified cliff sculpting as miniature composition; buildings and land are not missing.

issue: Named interlocking ceramic-border fidelity remains unresolved.
rationale: Mountain and tile border exist, but the independent review records unresolved ceramic contrast/interlocking/corners and lid-edge treatment in an explicitly partial v6 candidate. The board does not resolve that named detail beyond a soft geometric band. Retain substantive fidelity hold for the inlay, not solely the rose-versus-cream recolor; separate archive-byte hold remains untouched.

issue: Compact ochre dunes versus pale curled promotional ridges.
rationale: Dune silhouette and pale playa retain the desert identity. Accept simplified compact terrain and warmer palette; dark seam and uncertain hinge contact are not proven failure. This visual acceptance does not clear the separate source-archive inventory hold.
